hero.sub: He understands what makes Korean stories resonate - and translates them into the language of Hollywood.
hero.name: Kevin Nicklaus

kevin.lead: Kevin Nicklaus has spent decades in Hollywood adapting source IP for the screen. He built a long career at The Wolper Organization at Warner Bros., rising from Director of Development to Senior Vice President of Development at a single company. He has since advised Tapas Media and RIDI / Manta on the global expansion of Korean platform IP. He is currently Executive Producer on <title>The Beginning After The End</title> - a flagship Tapas webcomic now airing as a global anime on Crunchyroll and Fuji TV.

trust.intro: Kevin is still working inside Korean platforms today.
trust.rare: Few American producers advise two Korean platforms at once. For him, Korean IP isn't a passing trend - it's daily work.
trust.rights: He already understands - through the work itself - the environment Korean creators write in and the position they stand from. So when a Korean creator's first question at KStoryBridge is - <emph>"What happens to my rights?"</emph> - the answer is already built into where he begins.

expertise.p1: At The Wolper Organization, the production company at Warner Bros., Kevin spent decades focused on one thing - taking stories that already exist and bringing them to a new screen.
expertise.p2: Almost everything he has worked on has been IP with existing source material. Novels, comics, true stories, classics - the forms vary, but the common thread is one. Taking stories that already exist and re-drawing them on screen. His expertise comes down to a single word - adaptation.
expertise.p3: His development network reaches the major American and global studios and streamers. When a Korean story heads abroad, the people he already knows are the ones in the room.

hero.headlineLine1: Twenty-plus years connecting Korea and the world,
hero.headlineLine2: across every industry it had to be done in.
hero.sub: Internet services, smartphones, OTT, and now stories — the industries kept changing, but the work was always the same.
hero.name: Sungho Lee

lead.p1: Sungho Lee has spent over twenty years doing one job across many industries — connecting Korea and the world. He started in global internet services, running and bridging products at a time when those services were the new connective tissue between markets. He was there when Korean-built smartphones met Google's software and reached users across the planet. He led partnership work that helped Netflix find its footing in Asia. And at RIDI / Manta, he personally led the work of bringing Korean stories to Hollywood and to English-language readers.
lead.p2: What he is doing at KStoryBridge is the same job he had at RIDI / Manta — only this time not for one platform's catalogue, but for every Korean writer and rights-holder. While Kevin Nicklaus moves the work to the screen, Sungho builds every other path between a Korean story and the global decision-makers it needs to reach.

role.headlineLine1: The work he did at RIDI / Manta,
role.headlineLine2: now opening to all of Korea.
role.intro: What Sungho does at KStoryBridge is the same work he did at RIDI / Manta — only now, instead of one platform's catalogue, the path is open to any Korean writer, any platform, any work, no matter where it starts.
role.threeSeats: He carries three seats here at KStoryBridge.

hollywood.title: Connecting Korean writers and rights-holders to Hollywood
hollywood.description: The work he did at RIDI / Manta — the path a single Korean story takes to reach Hollywood — is now being laid out so that any Korean writer, on any Korean platform, can walk the same road.

kevin.title: The bridge between Kevin and Korea
kevin.description: Letting Kevin connect naturally with Korean writers, rights-holders, and platforms — whether the context is business or cultural — by carrying the words and tone of one side to the other. Possible because he has lived inside both.

business.title: Everything outside of content
business.description: Platform development and operations, contracts, payments, business systems — every area outside of making the work itself rests with him. The job of clearing every path outside the writing, so the writer can stay with the writing.

role.closingLine1: How a story is <emph>re-drawn for the screen</emph> — that's Kevin's work.
role.closingLine2: <emph>Every other path</emph> between Korea and the world — that's his.
role.closingLine3: That's why both seats sit together at KStoryBridge.

closing.line1: Kevin has spent his life moving writers' stories to the screen.
closing.line2: Sungho has spent over twenty years connecting Korea and the world.
closing.line3: KStoryBridge is what stands where the two of them meet.

rights.headline: Rights are protected from the start.
rights.body: Kevin is one of very few American producers working daily inside two Korean platforms — Tapas and RIDI / Manta. Sungho ran the same kind of work from the Korean side. So when a Korean creator's first question is <emph>"What happens to my rights?"</emph>, the answer is already built into where they begin.

path.headline: The road to Hollywood is already laid.
path.body: Kevin's development network reaches the major American and global studios and streamers, and his current credits — Crunchyroll, Fuji TV, Fangoria Studios — are proof that the road is real, not theoretical. Sungho is the one who puts the work onto that road, in language both sides will read correctly.
